title: STM32 HAL defines LL_PWR_STOP2_MODE instead of LL_PWR_MODE_STOP2 for U5 variant?
body:
All other HALs use `LL_PWR_MODE_STOP2`, but the U5 HAL uses the incredibly similar, but different, `LL_PWR_STOP2_MODE`.

This forces the creation of custom handlers for the U5 variant, our code base now contains...

```c
// Set STOP mode 2
#if defined(STM32U575xx)
  LL_PWR_SetPowerMode(LL_PWR_STOP2_MODE);
#else
  LL_PWR_SetPowerMode(LL_PWR_MODE_STOP2);
#endif
```

Also, this inconsistency created an unnecessary bug in the STM32LowPower library for the U5 variant.
https://github.com/stm32duino/STM32LowPower/commit/d2303da65831f1c4aeaafe7bc89833406a106ef8

Perhaps creating an alias in `stm32u5xx_ll_pwr.h` would preserve backward compatibility while bringing alignment on `LL_PWR_MODE_STOP2` across all HALs.

title: HAL_RCC_OscConfig(), incorrect flash latency when changing MSI frequency used as SYSCLK
body:
Hello,

In the current implementation of HAL_RCC_OscConfig(), there is a check to update
the flash latency before or after changing the MSI frequency when it is used as
SYSCLK. However, the implemented logic is reversed: increasing the MSI clock
range actually decreases its frequency. As a result, the flash latency is not
updated in the correct order.

I was able to reproduce the problem on a board based on STM32U5A5. An NMI
exception is triggered (caused by a FLASH ECC error) when MSI is used as SYSCLK
and its frequency is changed from 48 MHz to 12 MHz.

I fixed the issue locally by reversing the order between the flash latency update 
and the MSI frequency change in HAL_RCC_OscConfig(). I could share this patch if
needed.

comments.author: JavenZhou9481
KRASTM
comments.body:
Hello @JavenZhou9481,

I have checked with our team, and there is no known issue with the HAL_UARTEx_ReceiveToIdle_DMA() implementation. In normal mode, the function behaves as follows:

- It starts a DMA transfer for Size bytes.
- It receives data until either:
          Size bytes have been received (DMA complete), or
          an IDLE line event occurs before the buffer is full.
Then it calls HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback() with the actual number of bytes received. 

However, returning to your initial post where you shared a snippet of your code, I have a few comments:

You used HAL_UART_Transmit; is that a typo? Did you mean HAL_UART_Transmit_IT?
For osSemaphoreAcquire(rx_sem, timeout) == osOK, is the timeout long enough to receive all data?

With regards,

comments.author: JavenZhou9481
comments.body:
Hello 
The timeout for `osSemaphoreAcquire` is set at 1 seconds. Given that the actual baud rate is 9600 and the byte length is within 20 bytes, the timeout is more than sufficient.

My Buff length is 32 bytes, and the Size passed in is also 32 bytes, which is sufficient.

HAL_UART_Transmit is not misspelled. I didn't send data through IT and DMA, but I received data through DMA. Since my transmission is single-wire, I don't need to switch the direction of the serial port during the transmit completion interrupt (a lazy behavior).

I have disabled the DMA's half-transfer interrupt function now, and it works perfectly.

My transmission adheres to the MODBUS ASCII protocol.An indefinite length reception method is used, and a complete data frame is determined by checking for idle time. Upon sending ":010300010001(2Byte LRC)\r\n", I can successfully receive ":0103020000(2Byte LRC)\r\n". However, when sending ":0106000100AA(2Byte LRC)\r\n", I can observe from the oscilloscope's decoding and serial port tools that the reply ":0106000100AALRC\r\n" is fully received, but the MCU loses the '\n'

During debugging, I found that this particular response had entered a semi-transmitted interrupt state, so I disabled it.

This is all I can provide. The oscilloscope shows that the data is complete, and the hardware has ruled out any hardware link faults.

My current solution is
    Option 1: Disable DMA and only enable IT
    Option 2: Comment half-transmission interruptions callback

With regards,

comments.author: KRASTM
comments.body:
Hi again,

I think `Option 1: Disable DMA and only enable IT` is technically sound and a good choice for your use case. Just one clarification regarding the callbacks you registered and what you mentioned above:
> HAL_UART_Transmit is not misspelled. I didn't send data through IT and DMA, but I received data through DMA..... 

>HAL_UART_RegisterCallback(&huart4, HAL_UART_TX_COMPLETE_CB_ID, UART_TxCompleteCallback);

When you use blocking **HAL_UART_Transmit()**:

` HAL_UART_Transmit(&huart4, sdata, tlen, timeout);`

The transfer is completed by polling inside the function, and HAL_UART_TxCpltCallback (and therefore your UART_TxCompleteCallback) is **not** invoked by the HAL. This doesn’t cause any problem in your current design, but it means that any TX‑complete logic (for example, direction switching on a single‑wire link) placed in that callback will not be executed when using the blocking transmit API.

Please allow me to close the thread. Thank you for your understanding and for sharing your findings.

With regards,

title: LL_ADC_REG_StartConversion runs twice during HAL_ADC_Start
body:
I use ADC1 with discontinuous Mode (Num 1) and 2 channels:

My Read Pattern is very simple:

```c
HAL_ADC_Start()
HAL_ADC_PollForConversion()
HAL_ADC_GetValue() //ch1

HAL_ADC_Start()
HAL_ADC_PollForConversion()
HAL_ADC_GetValue() //ch2
```

But sometimes my channels swapped during read loop. I can even simulate this by adding extra `HAL_ADC_Start` during read loop.

I start digging into HAL_ADC_Start with debugger and find out that `HAL_ADC_Start` calls `LL_ADC_REG_StartConversion` twice:

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx-hal-driver/blob/5d9b26e77a3b40afc6cda07efdae4610c54319a1/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_adc.c#L1658

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx-hal-driver/blob/5d9b26e77a3b40afc6cda07efdae4610c54319a1/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_adc.c#L1681

Conversion started by first call to `LL_ADC_REG_StartConversion` can be ended before second call to `LL_ADC_REG_StartConversion` if task switched between this calls or interrupt occurred.

Since I use preemptive multithreading I have this situation once in a couple of days.

I thing `HAL_ADC_Start` need to call `LL_ADC_REG_StartConversion` exacly once.

title: GPDMA DMA state not reset when using negative block repeat address increments
body:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx-hal-driver/blob/38f1a11531ef7d76d0627a12bcf1378cb5c0bd6d/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_dma.c#L1073

At the end of a DMA transfer the source and destination block repeat sign is unchanged, hence bits 30 and 31 of the GPDMA BR1 register may be set at the end of the transfer. In this case, the test will fail and the HAL DMA state will not return to ready, despite completion.

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi @sk-waymont,

Looks like you're right. Thank you for this heads-up. the `WRITE_REG()` is defined at the [CMSIS](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-u5/blob/6e67187dec98035893692ab2923914cb5f4e0117/Include/stm32u5xx.h#L181) level as shown below:

```c
#define WRITE_REG(REG, VAL)   ((REG) = (VAL))
```

Instead, it should be replaced by the `SET_BIT()` macro defined as below:

```c
#define SET_BIT(REG, BIT)     ((REG) |= (BIT))
```

Let's have this fixed. I'll log an internal tracker.

With regards,

title: Usart reception on idle line event using dma with it disabled
body:
**Set up**

Board : custom board
Target : stm32u575vgt6
powered 3,3V

Dev env :
Clion 2024 & gcc Version 10.3-2021.10
HAL version 1.4

**USART DMA reception using HAL**
We have implemented the protocol Xmodem to perfom in app firmware update. For transfering data we use a serial communication.
The reception is trigered on idle event reception and the dma is in circular linked mode with half and completed interupt disabled.

it's more a case of a particular use than a bug.
When we use a dma to receive usart data without dma completed interrupt enabled, the HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback() is not called into the UART_IRQHandler() in case of the rbuffer is full. Consequently the data will be lost.

**Solution**
If DMA cplt disabled and buffer is full, modify the if condition to call the HAL_UARTEx_RxEventCallback() into  UART_IRQHandler().

title: HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady() NACK Bug
body:
Changes introduced in V1.5 of stm32u5xx_hal_i2c.c now mean that HAL_I2C_IsDeviceReady() will always return a HAL_ERROR immediately if a slave NACKs, without any repeated trials or a timeout.

After the START is generated (line #3480), a subsequent NACK will cause execution to drop out of the while loop and the intention is then to wait until the STOPF flag is reset (line #3535). Due to the if statement at #3513 we know that the NACK flag is definitely set when entering I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout().

A change to I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout for v1.5 at line #7292 now means that I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout() will call **I2C_IsErrorOccurred(), which returns HAL_ERROR if the NACK Flag is set**. We already know that the NACKF flag is set, that's why we've called I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout().

The above causes I2C_WaitOnFlagUntilTimeout() to return HAL_ERROR, which is treated as fatal at line #3535 which returns HAL_ERROR immediately without re-trying.

I don't think this is intended behaviour, as calling a function which return HAL_ERROR on a NACKF **because you've detected a NACKF** is pointless.

Also, it is normal for NACKs to be used by I2C devices to signal that they are busy as part of an ACK polling regime. See https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/en/devicedoc/21713m.pdf for one such example, where ACK polling is expected following a write to detect the end of EEPROM activity before the next transaction.

We're currently stuck in limbo between HAL versions, as V1.6 fixes some other bugs whilst introducing this one.
Can you confirm that it is safe to selectively downgrade stm32u5xx_hal_i2c.c and stm32u5xx_hal_i2c.h to v1.4 whilst upgrading the rest of HAL? I assume the API presented by stm32u5xx_hal_i2c.h is intended to be unchanged across HAL revisions?
Otherwise can you advise a fix?

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body: ST Internal Reference: 191244

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi @manisht-mwp,

According to our development teams, this is coded this way on purpose. Indeed, as you can see from [RM0456](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0456-stm32u5-series-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf), revision 5, there are two cryptographic instances: `AES` (chapter 49) and `SAES` (chapter 50).

The first instance, `AES`, is not intended to share any key. Instead, it is the second instance, `SAES`, the secure one, that could. Once the `SAES` instance shared its key with the `AES`, this latter handles that key as a normal one.

From a functions point-of-view:
* `CRYP_AES_Decrypt()`, along with `HAL_CRYP_Encrypt()`, are intended to be used by the `AES` instance, thus, setting the `AES_CR_KMOD` to `CRYP_KEYMODE_NORMAL`.
* `HAL_CRYPEx_EncryptSharedKey()` and `HAL_CRYPEx_DecryptSharedKey()`, on the other hand, are intended to be used by the `SAES` instance.

I hope this makes things clearer. Do not hesitate otherwise.

With regards,

title: header inclusion issues for STM32U545 series
body:
In trying to get Zephyr RTOS working on the Nucleo U545RE-Q board, I discovered header inclusion issues building the HAL for the STM32U545 SoC.

Zephyr RTOS makes use of the "stm32u5xx_hal_driver" for some interactions with the ST hardware, and builds the HAL by copying the default "stm32_hal_conf_template.h" to "stm32_hal_conf.h", leaving all options enabled.

However, some of the modules (specifically HAL_SRAM_MODULE_ENABLED, HAL_NAND_MODULE_ENABLED and HAL_NOR_MODULE_ENABLED) do not compile for the STM32U545.  Based on recommendations from a engineer in the Zephyr forums, I modeled changes to four files ((stm32u5xx_hal_sram.h, stm32u5xx_hal_nor.h, stm32u5xx_hal_nand.h and stm32u5xx_ll_fmc.h) with appropriate "#ifdef" checks using the example for the "stm32g4xx_hal_driver", and this allows the code to build for the U545 series.  Clearly, I'd appreciate ST (and others) review of these changes to ensure correctness.

I'll submit a PR shortly so the changes can be reviewed.

title: Asymmetric TX DMA for SPI causing a crash
body:
**Describe the set-up**

 * custom board
 * OZone

**Describe the bug (skip if none)**

I am interfacing a SPI graphics controller on STM32U585 and to update the frame buffer data, I have to send a single byte of command followed by n bytes as RGB data(more than 65532 bytes), however between I have to toggle a GPIO in between, which controls command/data mode.

To accomplish this, I am sending the single command byte by using **HAL_SPI_Transmit_IT**, and eventually I will toggle the GPIO and initiate the TX DMA transmission for RGB data on HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback and by using **HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA**(multiple iterations as the whole data is more than 65532 bytes which exceed the single shot of DMA).

Crash happens in the following line **as hspi->hdmarx is null** in time of comparison due to not using RX DMA.

[if (HAL_IS_BIT_CLR(cfg1, SPI_CFG1_TXDMAEN | SPI_CFG1_RXDMAEN) ||
        ((hspi->hdmarx) && (State != HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY_RX) && (hspi->hdmarx->Mode != DMA_LINKEDLIST_CIRCULAR)) ||
        ((hspi->hdmatx) && (State != HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY_TX) && (hspi->hdmatx->Mode != DMA_LINKEDLIST_CIRCULAR)))](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/6a00c6e1cc756c9804b3044dcd4238f5612adff0/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_spi.c#L2930)

**Additional context**
I have changed that comparison line as follow:

`    /* DMA Normal Mode */
    if (HAL_IS_BIT_CLR(cfg1, SPI_CFG1_TXDMAEN | SPI_CFG1_RXDMAEN) ||
        ((hspi->hdmarx) && (State != HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY_RX) && (hspi->hdmarx->Mode != DMA_LINKEDLIST_CIRCULAR)) ||
        ((hspi->hdmatx) && (State != HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY_TX) && (hspi->hdmatx->Mode != DMA_LINKEDLIST_CIRCULAR)))
`

but another issue I am facing now is that actually my DMA transmission will only work once and would fail in the second iteration as SPI state is not equal to HAL_SPI_STATE_READY in time of calling HAL_SPI_Transmit_DMA in HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback. It seems that SPI state would not be resetted in the second call of HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback which would happen the after completion of first DMA transmission.

Apparently, the following line of code would not get called at all to close the transfer:
[SPI_CloseTransfer](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/6a00c6e1cc756c9804b3044dcd4238f5612adff0/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_spi.c#L2968)

Actually after completion of first DMA transfer, SPI_CFG1_TXDMAEN is 1 so the comparison would fail and the aforementioned line would not get called.

I wonder if this is an edge case flaw? Or if I am not able to perform the **next DMA transfer in HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback** at all?

comments.author: ASELSTM
comments.body:
Hi @ramin-raeisi,

Regarding the first issue you have reported it has been already spotted and fixed internally.  The fix will be made available in the frame of a future release.

Concerning the second issue, the SPI state is updated to HAL_SPI_STATE_READY just after closing the transfer and clearing flags. 

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32u5xx_hal_driver/blob/6a00c6e1cc756c9804b3044dcd4238f5612adff0/Src/stm32u5xx_hal_spi.c#L2970

Thus, when calling `HAL_SPI_TxCpltCallback()` the SPI state is already set to **HAL_SPI_STATE_READY**. 

With regards,
